title: Home
content:
Welcome to Frame of Mind, a site for people who like to think a little harder about the films they watch, the books they read, and the lives they are living. This is not a place for jargon or gatekeeping. It is a place for clear, honest writing about the ideas that actually change how you see things.

Everything here is organized around five simple lenses. In Film & TV, we look past the plot to what a story is really doing. In Philosophy, we take the big questions out of the lecture hall and into everyday life. In Psychology, we explore why people think, feel, and act the way they do. In Books & Ideas, we sit with the works and thinkers worth knowing. And in Life & Meaning, we bring it all back to the question of how to live well.

Glad you are here — browse the latest posts below and see what grabs you.

title: About Frame of Mind
content:
Frame of Mind is a small, independent site for curious people who love films, big ideas, and understanding themselves and the world a little better. It was built around a simple belief: that philosophy, psychology, and serious film criticism do not need to be difficult or distant. They can be written in plain language, grounded in real life, and still be honest about the complexity underneath.

The five pillars

Everything we publish falls into one of five categories. Film & TV goes beneath the plot — why a particular cut lands, what a character's silence is doing, the idea a film is quietly arguing for. Philosophy takes a question like "what do we owe each other?" or "what makes a life meaningful?" out of the textbook and into ordinary decisions. Psychology looks at how the mind actually works — memory, habit, attention, the stories we talk ourselves into — and what the research does and does not support. Books & Ideas sits with the works and thinkers worth knowing, in essays meant to be read slowly. Life & Meaning is where it all comes together, connecting film, philosophy, and psychology to the practical question of how to live.

Who Frame of Mind is for

This site is for anyone who has ever finished a film or a book and actually wanted to talk about what it meant — no plot-summary recaps, no theory name-dropped to sound clever. It is for beginners who want a clear way in, and for readers already familiar with these subjects who appreciate writing that respects their time.

How we work

We hold our writing to a straightforward standard: it should be well researched, clearly reasoned, and honest about where an idea is settled and where it is still debated. When an interpretation is our own reading of a film or a book, we say so plainly rather than presenting opinion as fact. We also revisit older pieces and update them when we find a clearer or more accurate way to explain something.

Independent and reader-first

Frame of Mind is independent. Our essays and analysis reflect our own honest thinking, not the priorities of a sponsor, and we keep any advertising clearly separate from the writing you come here to read. Questions and ideas are always welcome at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.

Who writes Frame of Mind

Frame of Mind is written by Dasek Nahri, a writer focused on film, philosophy, and psychology. You can reach Dasek at {{WRITER_EMAIL}}, or the site at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.

title: About the Author
content:
Hi, I am Dasek Nahri, the writer behind Frame of Mind. I did not come to this through an academic career. I came to it the way a lot of people do: from watching a film that stayed with me longer than it should have, or reading a passage that quietly rearranged how I thought about something. That habit of paying attention is what I try to bring to every piece I publish here.

My interest in film, philosophy, and psychology started as separate curiosities, but over time I noticed they were really asking the same questions from different angles. A film explores an idea through story. Philosophy explores it through argument. Psychology explores it through evidence about how we actually think and behave. Frame of Mind exists because I wanted one place to hold all three conversations at once.

I write this site because I love the moment an idea finally clicks, when a concept stops sounding abstract and starts feeling useful. My goal is to get you to that moment faster. I read carefully, I try to represent films, books, and research fairly, and I am upfront when something I write is interpretation rather than settled fact.

When I am not writing, I am usually watching something worth thinking about, working through a book that has been on my list too long, or turning some ordinary decision into an excuse to think about philosophy. I believe good ideas do not have to be complicated to be worth your time, and that the best insights are often the ones that quietly change how you see the rest of your day.

I would genuinely love to hear from you, whether you have a question, a disagreement, or just want to say hello. You can read everything I have published here on the articles page. You can reach me anytime at {{WRITER_EMAIL}}.

title: Contact
content:
Frame of Mind is a small, independent site written and run by Dasek Nahri, and hearing from the people who read it is one of the best parts of the work.

Get in touch if you have a question about an essay, feedback on an analysis you disagreed with, or a correction. If a fact is wrong or an important angle is missing, tell me — that kind of note is often what makes the next version of a piece clearer. You can email the site at {{SITE_EMAIL}}, or reach me directly at {{WRITER_EMAIL}}.

I read every message and do my best to reply, usually within a few business days. Because this is a one-person project, a busy stretch can occasionally add a day or two, so thank you in advance for your patience.

A quick note on partnerships: to keep Frame of Mind independent and reader-first, I do not run sponsored essays, accept guest posts, or publish paid content dressed up as editorial, so pitches of that kind will not receive a reply. For anything else, though, please do reach out — I am always glad to hear from a fellow curious reader.

title: Privacy Policy
content:
Last updated: September 12, 2026

At Frame of Mind, we respect your privacy and want to be clear about how we handle information when you visit ibnbatoutaweb.com (the "Site"). This Privacy Policy explains what we collect, why we collect it, how it is used, and the choices you have. By using the Site, you agree to the practices described here.

Information we collect

We aim to collect as little personal information as possible. The information we do collect falls into a few categories:

  • Information you provide. When you email us or fill out a contact form, we receive your email address, your name if you share it, and the content of your message.
  • Analytics data. We collect anonymized or aggregated information about how visitors use the Site, such as which pages are viewed and how people arrive.
  • Log data. Like most websites, our servers automatically record standard technical information, including your IP address, browser type, device type, referring pages, and the date and time of your visit.
  • Cookies and similar technologies. We and our partners use cookies and comparable technologies to operate the Site, understand usage, and, where enabled, support advertising. See the sections below and our Cookie Policy for details.

How we use information

We use the information we collect to operate and improve Frame of Mind, to respond to messages you send us, to understand which content readers find helpful, to keep the Site secure and working properly, and to display advertising that helps fund the Site. We do not sell your personal information.

Cookies and web beacons

Cookies are small text files stored on your device that help a website function and remember certain information. Web beacons, also called pixel tags, are tiny graphics that help measure how content and ads are used. We use these technologies for essential Site functions, for analytics, and, where advertising is enabled, to help deliver and measure ads. You can control or delete cookies through your browser settings, though disabling some cookies may affect how the Site works.

Third-party advertising and Google AdSense

Frame of Mind may display advertising served by third-party vendors and ad networks, including Google. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies — such as Google's DoubleClick DART cookie — to serve ads based on a user's prior visits to Frame of Mind and other sites on the internet. Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on those visits.

You may opt out of personalized advertising, including the DART cookie, by visiting Google Ads Settings. You can also opt out of a third-party vendor's use of cookies for personalized advertising by visiting www.aboutads.info/choices and optout.networkadvertising.org.

For more information about how Google handles data, see Google's Privacy Policy and How Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services.

Analytics

We use analytics services to understand how visitors interact with the Site so we can improve our content. These services may set cookies and collect information such as pages visited, time on site, and general location derived from your IP address. This information is used in aggregate and helps us make Frame of Mind more useful.

Your privacy rights (GDPR, CCPA, and other US state laws)

Depending on where you live, you may have rights over your personal information under laws such as the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and similar privacy laws in other US states. These may include the right to access, correct, or delete the information we hold about you, the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information, the right to object to or restrict certain processing, and the right not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights. Frame of Mind does not sell your personal information for money; however, some data shared with advertising partners through cookies may be treated as a "sale" or "sharing" under certain US state laws, and where that applies you can opt out using the advertising controls described above. To make any privacy request, contact us at {{SITE_EMAIL}} and we will respond as required by applicable law.

Children's privacy

Frame of Mind is a general-audience site and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13, or under 16 where a higher age applies. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us and we will take appropriate steps to remove it.

Consent

By using the Site, you consent to this Privacy Policy. Where required by law, we ask for your consent before non-essential cookies, analytics, or personalized advertising are used, and you can withdraw or change your choices at any time.

Changes to this policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or for legal reasons. When we do, we will revise the "Last updated" date above. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

Contact

If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy or how your information is handled, please email us at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.

title: Cookie Policy
content:
This Cookie Policy explains how Frame of Mind uses cookies and similar technologies when you visit ibnbatoutaweb.com. It should be read alongside our Privacy Policy, which describes how we handle personal information more generally.

What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your device when you visit. They are widely used to make websites work, to remember your preferences, and to help site owners understand how their pages are used. Similar technologies, such as web beacons and pixels, serve related purposes. Cookies may be set by Frame of Mind directly, known as first-party cookies, or by third parties whose services we use, known as third-party cookies.

Types of cookies we use

  • Essential cookies. These are necessary for the Site to function properly, such as remembering your cookie preferences and keeping the Site secure. The Site cannot work correctly without them.
  • Analytics cookies. These help us understand how visitors use Frame of Mind, for example which pages are most popular and how people navigate the Site. We use this information in aggregate to improve our content.
  • Advertising cookies. Where advertising is enabled, these cookies help deliver ads, limit how often you see a given ad, and measure how well ads perform. Our advertising partners, including Google, may set cookies to serve ads based on your visits to this and other websites.

How to control cookies

You are in control of the cookies on your device. Most web browsers let you view, manage, block, and delete cookies through their settings. You can usually find these controls in the "Settings," "Preferences," or "Privacy" section of your browser. Please note that if you block or delete certain cookies, some parts of the Site may not work as intended. To opt out of personalized advertising specifically, you can also use the tools described in our Privacy Policy.

Consent

Where required by law, we ask for your consent before placing non-essential cookies, such as analytics and advertising cookies, on your device. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time through your browser settings or any cookie controls we provide on the Site.

Questions

If you have any questions about how Frame of Mind uses cookies, please email us at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.

title: Advertising & Consent
content:
Frame of Mind is a free, independent site, and advertising is one of the ways we cover the cost of running it. This page explains how advertising works here, who our partners are, and the choices you have over the ads you see. It works together with our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy.

Why we show ads

Hosting, tools, and the time it takes to research and write carefully all cost money. Displaying advertising lets us keep Frame of Mind free to read while remaining independent, so we never have to turn our writing into paid promotions. We aim to keep ads reasonable and clearly separate from the content you come here for.

Our advertising partners

When advertising is active, ads may be served by third-party partners, including Google AdSense. These partners use cookies and similar technologies to deliver ads, measure their performance, and, in some cases, personalize what you see based on your prior visits to this and other websites.

Personalized and non-personalized ads

Ads can be either personalized or non-personalized. Personalized ads use cookies and browsing information to show ads that may be more relevant to your interests. Non-personalized ads are based on general factors such as the content of the page or your approximate location, rather than your past browsing behavior. Where required, we will only show personalized ads with your consent.

Your consent and choices

For visitors in the EEA, the UK, and Switzerland, we collect consent through a Google-certified consent management platform (Google's Privacy & Messaging), and personalized advertising and non-essential cookies are used only after you grant it. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time through the same tool. Visitors in US states with their own privacy laws can exercise their choices as described in our Privacy Policy. You can also manage advertising choices directly through Google Ads Settings, www.aboutads.info/choices, and optout.networkadvertising.org.

Learn more

For full details on the information we collect and how cookies are used, please see our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy. If you have questions about advertising on Frame of Mind, email us at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.

title: Editorial Policy
content:
Frame of Mind publishes independent writing on film and TV, philosophy, psychology, books, and life and meaning. This Editorial Policy explains how our content is created, how we keep it trustworthy, and what you can expect from what you read here.

How we create content

Our essays are researched before they are published, drawing on the film or book itself, established philosophical and psychological sources, and, where relevant, credible reporting and research. Our analysis and interpretation of a film, a book, or an idea reflect the author's honest reading, informed by that research rather than by theory divorced from the work itself. When we discuss psychological findings, we aim to represent the underlying research fairly and to note where a topic is genuinely unsettled or debated.

Accuracy and sourcing

We take accuracy seriously. When we reference facts about a film's production, a philosopher's work, or a psychological study, we rely on reputable sources and aim to reflect the current understanding. Interpretation of art and ideas is not an exact science, so we try to explain our reasoning and to be upfront about where a claim is our own reading rather than settled fact.

Independence

Frame of Mind is independent, and our opinions are our own. Our essays and recommendations reflect our genuine thinking, not the priorities of any advertiser or brand. We do not publish paid or sponsored content disguised as editorial. If we ever feature a product or partnership, or if a post contains affiliate links, we will disclose it clearly so you always know what you are reading.

Corrections

We want our content to be as clear and accurate as possible, and we update posts when we find a better or more precise way to explain something. If you spot an error, whether it is a typo, an unclear argument, or a factual mistake, please let us know by emailing {{SITE_EMAIL}}. We review every report and will correct confirmed errors promptly.

Your trust

Everything on Frame of Mind is written with the goal of earning and keeping your trust. If we ever fall short of that, we want to hear about it.
meta_description: How Frame of Mind creates content: researched analysis of film, philosophy, and psychology, independent opinions, no hidden sponsored posts, clear corrections.

title: Content Disclaimer
content:
The information on Frame of Mind, including all essays, analysis, and commentary on film, TV, philosophy, psychology, and books, is provided for general information and entertainment purposes only. We share it in good faith to help you think more clearly and enjoy these subjects, but you engage with it at your own discretion.

Analysis, interpretation, and opinion

Our writing on film, TV, and books reflects the author's own interpretation. A film, a book, or a philosophical idea can reasonably be read in more than one way, and our essays present one considered perspective rather than a single correct answer. Similarly, our discussions of philosophy and psychology are intended to explain and explore ideas in an accessible way, not to present themselves as the final or only word on a topic.

Not professional advice

Frame of Mind is a site about film, philosophy, and psychology, not a source of professional psychological, medical, legal, or financial advice. Nothing on this Site should be taken as a substitute for guidance from a qualified professional. If you are dealing with a personal, psychological, legal, or financial matter, please consult a licensed professional who can consider your specific situation.

Advertising disclosure

Frame of Mind may display advertising, which helps support the Site and does not affect the honesty of our writing or recommendations. For more detail, please see our Advertising & Consent and Privacy Policy pages.

Contact

If you have any questions about this disclaimer, please email us at {{SITE_EMAIL}}.
